events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency finalized approval of Florida's state plan for implementing and enforcing emissions guidelines applicable to existing Commercial and Industrial Solid Waste Incineration (CISWI) units. events.title: Federal Acquisition Regulation: Inflation Adjustment of Acquisition-Related Thresholds

events.title: FEMA employees wrote to Congress warning of staffing crisis and retaliation
events.summary: On August 27, 2025, 182 employees of FEMA wrote to Congress in a document called the "Katrina Declaration" to warn that one-third of FEMA's full-time staff have separated from the agency this year, eroding institutional knowledge and relationships. events.title: Congress froze Washington, D.C. budget in March spending resolution
events.summary: In March 2025, Congress passed a continuing resolution to fund the government while freezing all federal spending. The resolution included Washington, D.C.'s budget, which is normally exempted from federal freezes because it is funded by local taxes, not federal funds. The House did not carve out the exemption, leaving the city with a $1.1 billion shortfall. The Senate unanimously approved a bill to fix the error, but the House never took it up. D.C. Mayor Muriel Bowser and local officials implemented a workaround but were forced to freeze hiring and cut contracts, grants, and expenditures across city agencies.
events.why_relevant: The budget freeze weakened D.C. services and created conditions that the administration later exploited to justify federal military deployment and takeover of the capital.

The approval covers MDAQMD Rule 1160, amended January 23, 2023, which regulates volatile organic compounds and nitrogen oxide emissions from internal combustion engines. The EPA also made administrative corrections to the Code of Federal Regulations and removed obsolete rules. The rule becomes effective September 29, 2025.

events.title: EPA publishes proposed consent decree establishing deadline for Kentucky ozone redesignation decision
events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency published notice of a proposed consent decree in Commonwealth of Kentucky v. U.S. EPA (W.D. Ky. No. 3:24-CV-600-CHB). Kentucky and the Louisville Metro Air Pollution Control District sued EPA for failing to timely approve or deny a request to redesignate the Kentucky portion of the Louisville ozone nonattainment area to attainment status under the 2015 8-hour ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standards. The proposed decree establishes a December 8, 2025 deadline for EPA to issue a final rule approving or denying the redesignation request, with notice and publication requirements. Public comment period closes September 29, 2025.
events.why_relevant: The consent decree resolves a Clean Air Act enforcement action and establishes binding deadlines for EPA regulatory action on air quality standards, affecting state-federal environmental governance and industrial compliance obligations.

events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency published notice of a proposed consent decree in Center for Biological Diversity and Center for Environmental Health v. Lee Zeldin (N.D. events.title: EPA solicits public comment on NASA's emergency exemption application for ortho-phthalaldehyde pesticide use on International Space Station
events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency announced receipt of NASA's application for a specific exemption under the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) section 18 to use ortho-phthalaldehyde (OPA) as a biocide in the International Space Station's internal active thermal control system coolant. OPA, an unregistered pesticide, would control aerobic and microaerophilic bacteria. NASA asserts OPA is the most effective alternative meeting safety and material-compatibility requirements. The chemical would be incorporated into a resin canister delivering up to 350 mg/liter over 8 hours, with concentrations degrading over 1–2 years, requiring periodic replenishment. EPA has authorized similar exemptions since 2011 and is soliciting public comment before deciding whether to grant the exemption.
events.why_relevant: The decision to grant or deny an emergency pesticide exemption for critical space infrastructure affects regulatory authority, public health oversight, and the precedent for unregistered chemical use in federal programs.

events.summary: The Federal Communications Commission adopted its fiscal year 2025 regulatory fee schedule, requiring collection of $390,192,000 in fees from telecommunications licensees and service providers. events.title: Noah Smith reviews Dan Wang's book "Breakneck" on China-U.S. governance differences
events.summary: Noah Smith publishes a book review of Dan Wang's "Breakneck," which argues that America is run by lawyers while China is run by engineers, explaining divergent development outcomes. Smith largely endorses Wang's thesis but raises alternative explanations: that the engineer-to-lawyer shift may be a natural phase of development, that communism rather than engineering culture drives Chinese planning, or that capital allocation becomes more important than mobilization as countries grow richer. Smith notes that the CCP Politburo has been shifting away from engineers toward social science majors until recently, and questions whether manufacturing dominance is sustainable for any wealthy nation.
events.why_relevant: The review engages substantive analysis of institutional and governance differences between democracies and authoritarian systems, contributing to public understanding of how different political structures shape policy outcomes and national development.
events.basis: Breakneck brings the same style Dan used in his annual letters, and uses it to elucidate a grand thesis: America is run by lawyers, and China is run by engineers.

events.title: FCC reinstates prior express written consent rule after court vacatur
events.summary: The Federal Communications Commission issued a final rule reinstating the prior version of 47 CFR 64.1200(f)(9) regarding prior express written consent requirements for telemarketing calls and text messages. The Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals vacated the Commission's 2023 revised rule on April 30, 2025. This ministerial order implements the court mandate without notice-and-comment rulemaking, effective immediately.

events.title: Trump administration ends de minimis tariff exemption for all countries
events.summary: The Trump administration ended the longstanding de minimis tariff exemption on Friday, August 29, 2025, eliminating duty-free entry for packages valued under $800. The exemption, established in the Tariff Act of 1930 and raised to $800 in 2015, had covered approximately 1.36 billion shipments annually. The White House cited protection of American manufacturers and national security concerns, claiming bad actors use the exemption to smuggle drugs. The change is expected to cost consumers up to $13 billion and disproportionately affect lower-income Americans and small overseas businesses.
events.why_relevant: The termination of de minimis exemption represents a major tariff policy shift that will increase costs for consumers, particularly lower-income households, and disrupt global e-commerce supply chains.
events.basis: A longstanding tariff exemption that let people skip import fees for small-value packages ended on Friday, leaving small businesses and postal services around the world scrambling to apply Donald Trump's tariffs to millions of shipments.

events.title: International postal service to U.S. collapsed due to tariff policy
events.summary: Postal traffic into the United States plunged by more than 80% after the Trump administration ended a tariff exemption for low-cost imports. Eighty-eight postal operators told the United Postal Union they suspended some or all postal service to the U.S. until a solution is implemented regarding U.S.-bound parcels valued at $800 or less. The UPU reported that global postal traffic to the U.S. fell 81% on August 29, 2025, compared with a week earlier, affecting nearly all 192 member countries.
events.why_relevant: A tariff policy change caused a near-total collapse of international postal service to the United States, disrupting commerce and communications.

events.title: Jim O'Neill appointed acting CDC director to advance RFK Jr vaccine policy agenda
events.summary: The White House appointed Jim O'Neill, a biotech investor and former Bush administration speechwriter with no medical training, as acting director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The appointment follows the firing of infectious disease expert Susan Monarez, who refused to resign under pressure from health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr and his allies. O'Neill's appointment is expected to advance Kennedy's goals of remaking federal vaccine policy. The move has prompted turmoil at the agency, with at least three top officials quitting in protest.
events.why_relevant: The appointment of an unqualified political operative to lead the nation's top public health agency, replacing a Senate-confirmed expert who resisted anti-vaccine directives, represents a direct attack on the independence and scientific integrity of federal public health institutions.
events.basis: The White House has chosen a top aide to health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr to temporarily lead the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention – an appointment that is expected to bolster Kennedy's goals of remaking federal vaccine policy.

events.title: Trump administration forced Social Security Administration Chief Data Officer Charles Borges to resign
events.summary: The Trump administration forced Charles Borges, Chief Data Officer at the Social Security Administration, to resign today. Borges had acted as a whistleblower identifying serious data breaches affecting more than 300 million Americans at risk of identity theft and loss of benefits. In his resignation letter, Borges stated he was leaving involuntarily after the administration made it impossible to perform his duties legally and ethically and caused him "serious attendant mental, physical, and emotional distress." Borges noted his service as an Active-Duty Naval Officer for over 22 years, decoration for valor in Operation Iraqi Freedom, and prior roles as a Presidential Innovation Fellow and CDC official during COVID.
events.why_relevant: Forced resignation of a whistleblower who identified critical security vulnerabilities represents retaliation against dissent and removal of oversight capacity protecting hundreds of millions of Americans.
